title: Integral ordinary and compact sections with perfect finite reductions
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and put $A_n=R/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], let $a_X:X\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and let $d\geq0$ be an integer with $\dim X\leq d$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$ in the derived-complete integral category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]; all integral tensors use its completed coefficient sheaf, rather than the discrete constant $R$. Suppose the derived reductions $K_n=K\otimes_R^LA_n$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction] have one Tor interval $[a,b]$, independent of $n$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Define the ordinary module complexes $C_*=R\Gamma(X,K)$ and $C_!=R\Gamma_c(X,K)$ by [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], using the integral direct images of [def-weil-derived-direct-image, def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. Then $C_*$ and $C_!$ belong to $D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(R)$ [def-weil-point-fg-complete-complexes] and are perfect [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. For every $n\geq1$, the canonical coefficient comparisons induce isomorphisms in $D(A_n)$
$$C_*\otimes_R^LA_n\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(X,K_n),\qquad C_!\otimes_R^LA_n\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_c(X,K_n).$$
Each of these reductions is isomorphic to a complex of finite free $A_n$-modules vanishing outside $[a,b+2d]$, with this single interval independent of $n$.

proof.text: For every positive exponent n+1, integral constructibility supplies intrinsic bounded constructibility of K_n. Its prescribed Tor interval is [a,b], and the Tor predicate itself implies a <= b, including zero inputs. Apply finiteCoefficientDirectImage_boundedConstructible_torAmplitude to the structure map, bundled over Spec k, to obtain intrinsic constructibility and [a,b+2d] for its ordinary image. Apply finiteCompactSupport_uniformTor_after_denseRefinement to the given compactification: its conclusions for the original compactification give intrinsic constructibility and exactly the same interval for the finite compact image. No nonemptiness or properness of X is required.

Apply point_tor_amplitude_realization to both finite point images in the interval [a,b+2d], using its finite-free-model clause. Rewrite the elementwise off-interval zero assertion as IsStrictlyGE a and IsStrictlyLE (b+2d). Its models use the small module localization, whereas the specified section comparison maps use the standard localization. Transport each model by Localization.uniq, the exact-section localization comparison sfSectionsCoefficientLiftIso, and Localization.compUniqFunctor. This retains the identical finite free complex and its bounds.

For a constructible integral point object N and q:N->Res(T), pointReductionUnitNormalization supplies an isomorphism chi from tensor of sections to sections of reduction with the specified scalar-unit equation. Put f=adjoint(q). The sheaf adjunction gives q=eta_N followed by Res(f). Evaluate the unit equation at N and apply naturality of the identity-on-sections restriction comparison to f. Injectivity of the module adjunction identifies the module adjunct of sections(q) with chi_N followed by sections(f). Thus it is invertible whenever f is, and composing with the localization isomorphism gives the very sfSectionsReductionFromProjection. For ordinary sections, unfold the actual chosen SfIntegralDirectImage: sfIntegralDirectImage_constructible proves its projection adjunct invertible. For compact sections, recover p and delta from the same derived-limit existence proof used by sfIntegralCompactSupportValue and sfSectionsCompactProjection; integralCompactSupport_prescribedReductions proves that projection adjunct invertible. This proves isomorphy of the specified maps. Compose their asIso isomorphisms with the finite models of the previous step, and handle either choice of C by substitution.

Each recorded integral section value already lies in pointFgComplete, so its cohomology has finite support and is finitely generated. The coefficient DVR theorem makes O_E a PID; transport the PID structure across ULift.ringEquiv. For each cohomology module choose a finite free surjection, using finite generation; Noetherianity gives finite presentation. Apply the PID-model clause of scalar_perfect_cohomology_and_pid_models to obtain perfectness of that module in degree zero. Convert the finite support to lower and upper integer bounds and apply isPerfectRingComplex_of_perfect_cohomology. This works directly in the recorded small localization and proves perfectness of both integral section values. It replaces the longer pseudo-coherence and maximal-fibre detour without changing the unit route.

The delivery creates 0 new nodes, keeps the statement and stmt_deps, and replaces an empty base proof (no re-split note applies). S1: lem-sf-integral-direct-image-constructible (field k, a_X:X->s, completed coefficients) and lem-coef-integral-compact-support (separated, dim<=d, uniform [a,b] -> [a,b+2d]) apply exactly. S2: K_n is in D^b_ctf by definition plus the hypothesis. cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale gives the bound [a,b+2d], and lem-sf-point-tor-amplitude-realization gives the finite free model of Fib_s = Gamma(s,-), which equals RGamma by def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology and def-weil-finite-coefficient-point(2). S3: point-sections-finiteness (2) gives D^b_fg. The lem-pod natural iso composed with the canonical direct-image comparisons gives the D(A_n) isos. Minor C3 remark, no change: the sentence identifying the point comparison quotes lem-pod's proof, and the statement's 'natural in N' iso is enough for the item. S4: O_E is a PID with maximal ideal (varpi), hence Noetherian (elementary). 066E gives pseudo-coherent and 068V(3)=>(1) with the A_1 bound gives perfect. Edge cases checked: X empty, d=0, n=1, torsion R/varpi input, nonproper X. No cycle: no cited node's closure reaches the item or its parent. Route: cited units are in the sk-thm-sf-package uses list, except lem-pod (sk-thm-sf-compatibility), a generic point-reduction tool use that I accept. The route departs from blueprint Step 2: Nakayama is replaced by existing D^b_fg finiteness plus the Stacks criteria, and the DVR tower by the existing reduction-isomorphism node; both are valid. Batch 5: lem-pod-point-sections-derived-reduction is a generic computation (made for prop-cohomological-finiteness, Milne 19.2), not a step of Poincare duality or the trace formula. Its closure holds only pod point-reduction helpers, and it is already in the closure of the base stmt_dep def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology. Accepted. No SGA citation.
